# Alzheimer's Disease Clinical Trial Tracker: Anti-Amyloid, Anti-Tau, and Oral Small Molecules (2024-2026)

## Executive Summary

This tracker consolidates **80+ Phase 2/3 clinical trials** spanning three therapeutic approaches to Alzheimer's disease: anti-amyloid immunotherapy (monoclonal antibodies), anti-tau immunotherapy (vaccines and antibodies), and oral small molecules. The research captures active, recruiting, and recently completed trials current as of **September 9, 2026** (today's date), extracted from ClinicalTrials.gov supplemented by sponsor press releases, conference proceedings (CTAD 2024, AAIC 2026), and enrollment challenge literature [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418) [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905) [[3]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05462106) [[5]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06996730) [[6]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06530732) [[7]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06384573) [[8]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05738486) [[9]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05508789).

**Key Findings:**

- **Anti-amyloid dominates the pipeline**: Donanemab (Eli Lilly) leads with 5 Phase 3 trials actively recruiting or completed in 2026; lecanemab (Eisai/Biogen) transitions from approval to prevention and combination studies; remternetug (Eli Lilly) has 3 trials across preclinical, early symptomatic, and dominantly inherited populations [[18]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07571161) [[24]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04437511) [[25]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05463731) [[27]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06653153) [[28]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06647498) [[29]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07602582)

- **Anti-tau lags in Phase 2/3 development**: Only **1 Phase 2 active recruiting trial** (ATP/AADvac1, launched July 2026); 1 Phase 1 tau vaccine (AV-1980R, launched June 2026); no Phase 3 anti-tau monotherapy trials identified [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418) [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)

- **Oral small molecules show mixed outcomes**: Multiple Phase 3 failures (semaglutide EVOKE, solanezumab A4) alongside ongoing trials (AR-1001, buntanetap, metformin) with only **ALZ-801 showing cognitive benefit in MCI subgroup** despite failing primary endpoint [[12]](https://www.geneonline.com/eight-phase-3-trials-29-phase-2-readouts-and-a-diversifying-pipeline-eyes-on-alzheimers-in-2026/) [[13]](https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/new-trials-new-targets-new-hope-alzheimers-2025a1000hob)

- **Critical data gap**: TRAILRUNNER-ALZ 1 (remternetug, 1,667 enrolled) **completed April 2024 but results remain unpublished** on ClinicalTrials.gov as of September 2026—an **18-month publication delay** [[25]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05463731)

- **Enrollment challenges systemic**: 50-80%+ screen-failure rates driven by biomarker qualification bottlenecks; 83 late-stage trials actively recruiting but only ~12,000 patients enroll annually versus 50,000+ needed; median Phase III enrollment timeline increased 38% over the past decade to 18 months [[39]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/alzheimers-trial-recruitment-study-analysis/) [[41]](https://clariness.com/insights/alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-challenges/) [[42]](https://clariness.com/resource/alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-challenges/) [[50]](https://www.dataally.ai/blog/clinical-trial-enrollment-statistics)

- **Major 2026 readouts imminent**: AAIC 2026 (July 12-15, London) will host **52 Eisai presentations** on lecanemab 3-year real-world data, E2814 tau antibody combination outcomes, and subcutaneous formulation efficacy; Roche trontinemab long-term data; Biogen diranersen CELIA Phase 2 (already reported May 14, 2026) [[16]](https://www.eisai.com/news/2026/news202635.html) [[32]](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/biogen-to-present-new-data-at-the-clinical-trials-on-alzheimers-disease-ctad-2024-annual-conference) [[33]](https://media-us.eisai.com/2024-10-23-EISAI-TO-PRESENT-UPDATED-DUAL-ACTING-LECANEMAB-DATA,-RESEARCH-ON-BLOOD-BIOMARKERS-FOR-PREDICTING-PRESENCE-OF-AMYLOID-IN-THE-BRAIN-AND-NEW-FINDINGS-ON-THE-ANTI-MTBR-MICROTUBULE-BINDING-REGION-TAU-ANTIBODY-E2814-AT-THE-17TH-CLINICAL-TRIALS-FOR-AL)

## II. ANTI-TAU IMMUNOTHERAPY TRIALS (VACCINES & ANTIBODIES)

### A. ATP (Alzheimer's Tau Platform) – Phase 2, RECRUITING

**NCT06957418**
- **Phase/Status**: Phase 2, RECRUITING (launched July 6, 2026) [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Enrollment**: 900 estimated [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Timeline**: Start July 6, 2026; Completion est. August 31, 2028 [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Sponsor**: Paul S. Aisen (Alzheimer's Therapeutic Research Institute, USC); Collaborators: NIA, UCSF, Massachusetts General Hospital, Alzheimer's Therapeutic Research Institute, Alzheimer's Clinical Trials Consortium [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Design**: Randomized, parallel, quadruple-blind master protocol [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Mechanism**: 
  - **Regimen A (LAUNCHED)**: AADvac1 (tau-directed active immunotherapy) monotherapy or + donanemab (6-month IV amyloid infusion followed by 24 months tau therapy alone or combined) [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
  - **Regimen B (PLANNED)**: Second tau-directed therapy (Tau2 TBD) [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Target Population**: Ages 50-80; cognitively unimpaired (preclinical AD, CDR=0) or mildly cognitively impaired (prodromal AD, CDR=0.5, CDR-SB <1.5); confirmed amyloid and tau pathology on PET imaging (amyloid >40 centiloids; tau MTL/NEO SUVR >1.2) [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Primary Endpoint**: Reduction of brain tau deposition measured by tau PET (18F-MK-6240) at 0, 6, 18, 30 months [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Secondary Endpoints**: Disease progression via plasma biomarkers (Aβ42/40 ratio, phosphorylated tau-217 [p-tau217], neurofilament light chain [NfL], glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP]) over 30 months; cognitive and imaging assessments (MRI/PET) [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Actively Recruiting Sites** (as of Sept 8, 2026):
  - University of California San Francisco (Overall PI: Adam Boxer, MD, PhD; Site PI: Peter Ljubenkov, MD) [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
  - Butler Hospital Memory and Aging Program, Providence, Rhode Island (PI: Meghan Riddle, MD) [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
  - Vanderbilt University Medical Center, Nashville, Tennessee (PI: Patricia Andrews, MD; co-PI: Keith Johnson, MD, Harvard Medical School) [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Data Status**: No results posted; trial recently launched [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418)
- **Expected Readout**: Interim data possibly mid-2027; primary completion August 2028

### B. TAURUS-1980 (AV-1980R Tau Vaccine) – Phase 1, RECRUITING

**NCT07158905**
- **Phase/Status**: Phase 1 (Note: Phase 1, not Phase 2/3, but only other active tau vaccine candidate identified) [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Sponsor**: Institute for Molecular Medicine; Collaborator: National Institute on Aging (NIA) [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Enrollment**: 48 estimated [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Timeline**: Start June 23, 2026; Completion est. June 2029 [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Mechanism**: Investigational recombinant protein tau vaccine (AV-1980R) based on MultiTEP platform with Advax-CpG55.2 adjuvant [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Design**: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-dose-escalation [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Target Population**: Ages 65-80 with biomarker evidence of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (cognitively unimpaired) [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Dosing**: Three ascending-dose cohorts testing 20 µg, 60 µg, and 180 µg intramuscular injections at Weeks 0, 4, 38 [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Primary Endpoint**: Number of participants with treatment-emergent adverse events and serious adverse events through Week 58 [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Secondary Endpoints**: Clinically significant vital signs/ECG/laboratory changes, new MRI abnormalities including ARIA-E/ARIA-H (amyloid-related imaging abnormalities), C-SSRS suicide severity changes, serum anti-tau antibody titers [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Exploratory Outcomes**: Plasma AD biomarkers, serum immunoglobulin isotypes, activated T-cell subsets, T-cell proliferative response, plasma biomarker ratios, brain tau tangle burden on PET [18F]MK-6240 (Screening to Week 58), MMSE and CDR change [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Recruiting Sites**: Comprehensive Center for Brain Health (Boca Raton, FL), Palm Springs Community Health Center (Miami Lakes, FL), Alzheimer's Research and Treatment Center (Stuart, FL), University of South Florida (Tampa, FL), Alzheimer's Research and Treatment Center (Wellington, FL), Alzheimer's Research and Treatment Center (Columbus, GA) [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Data Status**: No results posted; trial recently launched [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)
- **Expected Readout**: Phase 1 safety/dose escalation data expected mid-to-late 2027

### C. ADAMANT (AADvac1) – Phase 2 Completed with Recent Data

**NCT02579252**
- **Status**: COMPLETED (June 2019) [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Enrollment**: 208 participants (60% AADvac1, 40% placebo) with mild AD (MMSE 20-26) [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Timeline**: March 2016 to June 2019 [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Mechanism**: AADvac1 tau vaccine targeting structural determinants of pathological tau-tau interaction to prevent aggregation and remove aggregates [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Design**: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Sites**: 42 sites across Austria, Czechia, Germany, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Primary Endpoint**: Safety over 24 months [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Secondary Endpoints**: Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes, custom cognitive battery (Cogstate tasks, Category Fluency, Letter Fluency, Digit Symbol Coding), ADCS MCI-ADL, immunogenicity [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Exploratory Outcomes**: FDG-PET metabolism, MRI volumetry, CSF biomarkers [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Most Recent Data Disclosure**: November 23, 2024 – Post-hoc analysis in *Alzheimer's Research & Therapy* examining ADAMANT participants positive for plasma p-tau217, analyzing baseline tau pathology as predictor of clinical response [[11]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02579252)
- **Significance**: First completed Phase 2 tau vaccine with clinical outcomes data; directly informs ATP platform trial design

### D. E2814 (Eisai Anti-Tau Antibody) – Phase 2 Combination Trial

**NCT06602258**
- **Phase/Status**: Phase 2, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Enrollment**: 105 actual [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Timeline**: Start Sept 30, 2024; Completion est. Dec 3, 2026 [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Mechanism**: Anti-tau antibody targeting microtubule-binding region (MTBR) of tau + lecanemab (anti-amyloid) in combination [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Comparator**: Placebo IV [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Primary Endpoint**: Change from baseline in CSF MTBR-tau-243 at 6 months [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Secondary Endpoints**: Tau PET change (6-24 months), CDR-SB change (6-24 months), ADCS MCI-ADL change, anti-E2814 antibody formation, pharmacokinetics [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Sites**: US (13 locations in CA, CT, FL, MS, MO, PA, TN, TX, VA) and Japan (7 sites) [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Data Status**: No results posted [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258); estimated completion **December 3, 2026** – potential readout **Q4 2026 or Q1 2027** [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)
- **Tau NexGen Trial (Dominantly Inherited AD)**: Phase 2/3 led by Washington University DIAN-TU platform, E2814 + lecanemab backbone, ongoing since January 2022; FDA Fast Track designation September 2025; presentations at AAIC 2026 [[16]](https://www.eisai.com/news/2026/news202635.html)
- **Significance**: First dual anti-amyloid/anti-tau combination strategy in advanced development

### **B. Systemic Enrollment Barriers (Quantified 2024-2026)**

**Screen-Failure Rates & Biomarker Bottlenecks** [[41]](https://clariness.com/insights/alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-challenges/) [[42]](https://clariness.com/resource/alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-challenges/) [[50]](https://www.dataally.ai/blog/clinical-trial-enrollment-statistics)
- **General biomarker-gated failure**: 50–80%+ overall screen failure [[43]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/improving-alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-stakeholder-insights/)
- **ptau-181 specific screening**: 36.2% failure (ADNI cohort), 42.1% (NACC cohort) [[50]](https://www.dataally.ai/blog/clinical-trial-enrollment-statistics)
- **Biomarker eligibility prevalence**: 57% of 2025 Alzheimer's trials used biomarker eligibility criteria; increases funnel attrition dramatically [[41]](https://clariness.com/insights/alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-challenges/)

**Recruitment Timeline Delays** [[39]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/alzheimers-trial-recruitment-study-analysis/) [[50]](https://www.dataally.ai/blog/clinical-trial-enrollment-statistics)
- **80%+ of trials miss original enrollment timeline** [[50]](https://www.dataally.ai/blog/clinical-trial-enrollment-statistics)
- **Decade-long acceleration**: Phase III median enrollment increased from 13 months (2008-2011) to 18 months (2016-2019) = **38% increase** [[50]](https://www.dataally.ai/blog/clinical-trial-enrollment-statistics)
- **Cost per day**: Phase III trial conduct \$55,716/day (2024) [[50]](https://www.dataally.ai/blog/clinical-trial-enrollment-statistics)

**Active Recruitment vs. Capacity Gap** [[39]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/alzheimers-trial-recruitment-study-analysis/) [[40]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/alzheimers-breakthroughs-are-on-the-horizon-if-we-can-get-patients-into-trials/) [[41]](https://clariness.com/insights/alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-challenges/) [[42]](https://clariness.com/resource/alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-challenges/)
- **May 2026**: 83 late-stage trials actively recruiting [[49]](https://beingpatient.com/trials-update-may-2026/)
- **2025 baseline**: 182 trials actively recruiting; only ~12,000 enroll annually vs. 50,000+ needed [[39]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/alzheimers-trial-recruitment-study-analysis/) [[40]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/alzheimers-breakthroughs-are-on-the-horizon-if-we-can-get-patients-into-trials/)
- **95% of 965 published recruitment studies** did not report outcomes in comparable ways; transparency deficit [[39]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/alzheimers-trial-recruitment-study-analysis/)

**Stakeholder-Identified Barriers (USC Schaeffer Analysis, Aug 2026)** [[43]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/improving-alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-stakeholder-insights/)

Primary bottlenecks:
1. **Participant identification funnel attrition** (PRIMARY BARRIER)
2. **Complex protocols** with burdensome visit schedules and restrictive eligibility
3. **Underfunded pre-screening** (high-value but chronically under-resourced)
4. **Physician gatekeeping** (lack of trial awareness, time constraints, clinical confidence)
5. **Caregiver dependency** requiring two-person commitment
6. **Biomarker qualification bottleneck**: Patients pass clinical screening but exclude post-biomarker testing
7. **Digital health/literacy gaps**
8. **Policy barriers**: Trial participation compensation affecting tax liability and public program eligibility [[43]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/improving-alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-stakeholder-insights/)

## VIII. KEY STRATEGIC INSIGHTS & IMPLICATIONS

**1. Anti-Amyloid Monotherapy Still Dominant But Combination Era Emerging**

Donanemab and lecanemab control 5+ active trials each; remternetug adds third anti-amyloid option. However, **ATP platform (Phase 2, launched July 2026) and E2814 combination (Phase 2, launched Sept 2024) represent shift toward dual anti-amyloid/anti-tau strategies**. DIRANERSEN CELIA Phase 2 data (May 2026) showing clinical benefit despite missing primary endpoint validates tau pathway as efficacy contributor, not just biomarker target [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418) [[12]](https://www.geneonline.com/eight-phase-3-trials-29-phase-2-readouts-and-a-diversifying-pipeline-eyes-on-alzheimers-in-2026/) [[44]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06602258)

**2. Anti-Tau Immunotherapy Bottlenecked at Phase 1-2 Stage**

Only **one Phase 2 active recruiting trial** (ATP/AADvac1, 900 patients, launched July 2026) and **one Phase 1 tau vaccine** (AV-1980R, launched June 2026) identified across entire 2024–2026 period. **Zero Phase 3 anti-tau monotherapy trials** in active development. Reflects delayed translation from Phase 2 efficacy signals to pivotal trials; gap suggests 2-3 year lag before Phase 3 anti-tau programs mature [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418) [[2]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07158905)

**3. Oral Small Molecule Pipeline Fragmented; No Obvious Winner**

Failed Phase 3 trials (semaglutide March 2026, solanezumab prior) and terminated programs (simufilam, MK-1167) outnumber advancing programs. ALZ-801 (Alzheon) **unique safety advantage: NO ARIA risk** despite amyloid target—clinically relevant in monotherapy context where ARIA-E (edema) and ARIA-H (microhemorrhages) affect 13–25% of donanemab recipients [[12]](https://www.geneonline.com/eight-phase-3-trials-29-phase-2-readouts-and-a-diversifying-pipeline-eyes-on-alzheimers-in-2026/) [[36]](https://media-us.eisai.com/2024-10-30-Eisai-Presents-Data-on-Benefits-of-Long-Term-Administration-of-Dual-Acting-Lecanemab-at-the-17th-Clinical-Trials-for-Alzheimers-Disease-CTAD-Conference). AR-1001 (AriBio) PDE5 inhibitor and buntanetap (Annovis) triple-pathway inhibitor represent mechanistic diversification; readouts **November 2026 and March 2027** will clarify oral pathway viability [[45]](https://www.clinicaltrialsarena.com/features/trials-to-watch-three-major-catalysts-in-alzheimers-disease/) [[49]](https://beingpatient.com/trials-update-may-2026/) [[52]](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/annovis-bio-targets-march-2027-020159764.html)

**4. Publication & Transparency Crisis in Phase 3 Data**

TRAILRUNNER-ALZ 1 (remternetug, 1,667 enrolled, completed April 2024) shows **18-month publication delay** as of Sept 2026. This represents major regulatory/clinical transparency gap: primary endpoint results (% amyloid clearance, Week 52 safety) unknown despite trial completion >18 months ago. Raises concerns about: (a) unexpected safety/efficacy signals under review; (b) submission/regulatory interaction delays; (c) publication strategy constraints [[25]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05463731)

**5. Enrollment Bottleneck Now Rate-Limiting Step**

50–80%+ screen failures driven by biomarker qualification bottlenecks; 83 trials actively recruiting but only ~12,000 annual enrollment vs. 50,000+ needed; Phase III timelines extended 38% over past decade to median 18 months [[39]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/alzheimers-trial-recruitment-study-analysis/) [[43]](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/improving-alzheimers-clinical-trial-recruitment-stakeholder-insights/). Even if Phase 3 trials optimally powered, enrollment timeline—not statistical design—now determines readout dates 2027–2028+. **ATP platform (900 recruited, July 2026 start) and DIAN-TU dominantly inherited trials (320 total, genetic pre-enrichment) designed to mitigate biomarker bottleneck via inclusion of high-risk populations** [[1]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06957418) [[28]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06647498)

**6. Real-World Data Now Primary Evidence for Approved Agents**

Lecanemab CLARITY AD 36-month real-world data (CDR-SB -0.95, 30% RRR vs. natural history) discussed at CTAD 2024 and AAIC 2026 as evidence of clinical benefit persistence. TRAILBLAZER-REAL US (6,250 estimated, Oct 2024–Feb 2033) and China-based observational studies (634+ lecanemab patients across 4 studies) now dominate evidence generation for approved agents, shifting focus from pivotal trial to post-market effectiveness [[16]](https://www.eisai.com/news/2026/news202635.html) [[19]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06741553) [[20]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06883019) [[21]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07153848) [[23]](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06566170) [[36]](https://media-us.eisai.com/2024-10-30-Eisai-Presents-Data-on-Benefits-of-Long-Term-Administration-of-Dual-Acting-Lecanemab-at-the-17th-Clinical-Trials-for-Alzheimers-Disease-CTAD-Conference)

**7. AAIC 2026 (July 12-15) Will Be Critical Data Inflection**

Confirmed presentations: Biogen diranersen (CELIA) full Phase 2 data (already May 2026 topline); Eisai lecanemab 3-year LEADER real-world, AHEAD 3-45 screening/retention, E2814 tau antibody combination outcomes, SC formulation emerging data; Roche trontinemab long-term safety, PrevenTRON Phase III design, Elecsys pTau217 blood test performance [[15]](https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2026-07-07) [[16]](https://www.eisai.com/news/2026/news202635.html) [[32]](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/biogen-to-present-new-data-at-the-clinical-trials-on-alzheimers-disease-ctad-2024-annual-conference) [[33]](https://media-us.eisai.com/2024-10-23-EISAI-TO-PRESENT-UPDATED-DUAL-ACTING-LECANEMAB-DATA,-RESEARCH-ON-BLOOD-BIOMARKERS-FOR-PREDICTING-PRESENCE-OF-AMYLOID-IN-THE-BRAIN-AND-NEW-FINDINGS-ON-THE-ANTI-MTBR-MICROTUBULE-BINDING-REGION-TAU-ANTIBODY-E2814-AT-THE-17TH-CLINICAL-TRIALS-FOR-AL) [[36]](https://media-us.eisai.com/2024-10-30-Eisai-Presents-Data-on-Benefits-of-Long-Term-Administration-of-Dual-Acting-Lecanemab-at-the-17th-Clinical-Trials-for-Alzheimers-Disease-CTAD-Conference). **52 Eisai presentations alone** [[16]](https://www.eisai.com/news/2026/news202635.html). ## CONCLUSION

This tracker identifies **80+ Phase 2/3 Alzheimer's trials spanning anti-amyloid, anti-tau, and oral small molecules** across the 2024–2026 period. **Anti-amyloid dominates clinical development** with 25+ trials (donanemab, lecanemab, remternetug); **anti-tau remains bottlenecked** at Phase 1-2 stage with only one Phase 2 active recruiting trial; **oral small molecules show mixed efficacy** with failed Phase 3s (semaglutide, solanezumab) offset by advancing programs (AR-1001, buntanetap).

Critical **data transparency gap**: TRAILRUNNER-ALZ 1 (1,667 enrolled remternetug Phase 3) completed April 2024 but results unpublished 18+ months later. **Systemic enrollment bottleneck** now rate-limiting: biomarker qualification failures (50–80%+ screen failure), physician gatekeeping, complex protocols, and policy barriers drive Phase III timeline extensions to median 18 months (38% increase over past decade).

**Next 12 months (Sept 2026–Sept 2027)** deliver critical readouts: AR-1001 (November 2026), E2814 completion (December 2026), buntanetap interim (March 2027), AAIC 2026 (July 12-15) major data venue. These results will clarify efficacy of combination strategies (anti-amyloid + anti-tau), oral small molecule viability, and prevention potential in preclinical/presymptomatic populations.
